answer: Why does the saffron merchant trust one stall, not ten? Each mask must dye its bond in saffron, stamped only when the comet passes — a rare sky the network opens once, so no clone army can mint bonds in bulk. One honest player stakes 100, weight 100. Split into ten masks and each must pay the full 100 bond yet earns weight 1: tenfold cost, one-tenth the voice. The fable ends the same: I keep one mask, one bond, and let counterfeiters pay for their own costumes.
